title: A four-period Tau Ceti model fitted to HARPS raises HIRES error by 4.8 to 6.3 percent in four noise models
abstract: We test whether four fixed circular waves transfer between public HARPS and HIRES velocities of Tau Ceti. We fit periods of 20.00, 49.41, 162.87, and 636.13 days in 507 HARPS nightly averages and test the fixed coefficients in 268 HIRES nightly averages. The model increases weighted HIRES squared error by 4.85 to 6.34 percent with two extra noise levels and with or without an annual baseline wave. In the main model, separate 30-day block sampling in both instruments gives a 95 percent gain interval of -15.75 to -0.65 percent. An annual baseline gives -14.01 to +0.23 percent. Reverse transfer also increases error. Each single-period interval includes zero. Simulations show limited sensitivity to weak coherent waves. The result does not reject the candidates: fixed periods, circular orbits, correlated noise, and shared discovery observations limit the test. No new planet is found. The bundle includes original code, aggregate results, a figure, input hashes, and separate-scratch retrieval steps. External observation records are not bundled.

display.caption: Frozen four-period HARPS models increase HIRES error in four noise tests. Intervals resample both instruments in 30-day blocks.
